Financial_Insti.name: PhilHealth
Financial_Insti.description: PhilHealth is the Philippines' government-owned health insurer, providing universal health coverage through a social insurance program. It pools funds from member contributions to subsidize medical costs, making healthcare affordable for hospitalizations and preventive care.

branches.location: Valgosons Building, Bolton Extension, Poblacion, Davao City

programs.program_description: Government program that helps Filipinos take care of their health and prevent illness. YAKAP Clinics watch over members' health, find illness early, and give the right medicines so the illness does not get worse and hospital stays are avoided.

benefits.benefit_name: Primary Care Checkup

Selected laboratory tests based on risk, age and health assessment: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with Platelet Count, Lipid Profile, Fasting Blood Sugar (FBS), Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT), Hemoglobin Test (HbA1c), Creatinine, Chest X-Ray, Sputum Microscopy, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Urinalysis, Pap Smear, Fecalysis, Fecal Occult Blood Test (FOBT), Upper Abdomen & Pelvic Ultrasound
Medicines under PhilHealth GAMOT
Breast cancer screening: Breast Ultrasound & Mammogram
Liver cancer screening: Alpha Fetoprotein Test & Liver Ultrasound
Colorectal cancer screening: Fecal Immunochemical Test, Fecal Occult Blood Test & Colonoscopy
Lung cancer screening: Low-dose Chest CT Scan

requirements.requirement_description: PhilHealth Identification Number (PIN) with updated membership

procedure.instruction: Register: make sure you have a PhilHealth Identification Number (PIN) and your membership is updated.
Choose a YAKAP Clinic using the eGovPH Super App, the PhilHealth Member Portal, or the nearest PhilHealth office.
Have your First Patient Encounter (FPE): medical history, health screening and health education.
Sign the form agreeing that your chosen YAKAP Clinic will keep caring for you.
Keep seeing your YAKAP doctor for prescriptions, referrals for laboratory and/or cancer screening tests when needed, and follow-up checkups.

programs.program_name: Z Benefits: Breast Cancer (cStage 0 to IV)
eligibility: PhilHealth members and their qualified dependents who are eligible to avail of PhilHealth benefits at the time of pre-authorization approval

Breast cancer clinical stage requiring treatments covered under the Z Benefits (Stage 0 Ductal Carcinoma in Situ (DCIS), Stage I, Stage II, Stage III or Stage IV), with management involving any or all of: Surgery; Chemotherapy (neo/adjuvant); Targeted therapy; Hormonotherapy; Surveillance
Chemotherapy (neo/adjuvant): patient has not initiated any chemotherapy treatment from any HF

Diagnostic tests are covered when all of these are met: Positive (+) breast mass AND/OR palpable axillary lymph node; BI-RADS category 4 to 5 result of either mammogram or ultrasound; and Biopsy result of confirmed malignant breast cancer or ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS)
programs.program_description: PhilHealth's Z Benefit package for breast cancer, up to P1.4 million (effective March 30, 2024). It covers diagnostic tests, surgery, hormonotherapy, chemotherapy, targeted therapy and surveillance after surgery, at Z Benefits contracted health facilities. Up to five (5) days are deducted from the 45-day annual benefit limit.

benefits.benefit_name: Total package
Diagnostic tests and prognostication
Surgical procedures (partial mastectomy to modified radical mastectomy)
Hormonotherapy
Cytotoxic chemotherapy
Targeted therapy
Surveillance
No co-payment for patients admitted in basic or ward-type accommodation

procedure.instruction: Regardless of the type of cancer, bring your PhilHealth ID to the hospital's Z Benefits coordinator for the list of requirements and further steps.

Financial_Insti.name: Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO)
Financial_Insti.description: Government agency that gives financial help to people with health problems through its Medical Assistance Program, together with government and private hospitals, health facilities and medicine retailers.

eligibility: Individuals with health-related problems seeking financial help
programs.program_description: Financial help for patients, given in partnership with government and private hospitals, health facilities, medicine retailers and other partners. Cancer treatment (chemotherapy drugs, immunotherapy and radiation therapy) is one of the types of help. If approved, the patient gets a Guarantee Letter (GL) for the hospital, health facility, medicine retailer or diagnostic center.

benefits.benefit_name: Cancer treatment: chemotherapeutic drugs and immunotherapy
Radiation therapy
Confinement assistance
Laboratory, diagnostic and imaging procedures (such as CT-Scan, MRI, PET Scan and biopsy)

requirements.requirement_description: Valid proof of identity of the patient (government-issued ID or other accepted ID)
Valid ID of the patient's next of kin, if applicable

For cancer treatment: updated clinical or medical abstract (issued within the past 3 months), medical prescription, and treatment protocol (chemotherapy) or treatment plan (radiation therapy), each with the full name, signature and license number of the attending physician
For cancer treatment: one quotation from the hospital willing to accept the GL, or official quotations from three different suppliers if the medicine is not available in the hospital

procedure.instruction: Go to www.pcso.gov.ph, select "E-Services", then "Online MAP Application", and create an account.
Log in with your name, date of birth and email, and enter the one-time code sent to your email.
Click "Apply Now", choose the partner health facility, its city and the type of request, then get a queuing number.
Upload all required documents as PDF files (not more than 2MB each) and submit the application.
Wait for the result in your email or in your online account.

Financial_Insti.name: Department of Health (DOH)
Financial_Insti.description: National government department for health. Its MAIFIP program helps pay the medical bills of patients who cannot afford them.

branches.location: PRRD Bldg Bajada, Davao City (infront SPMC Hospital)

programs.program_name: Medical Assistance for Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP)
eligibility: Indigent and financially incapacitated patients who cannot afford their medical expenses
Including PhilHealth members whose remaining bill is still too big
programs.program_description: Covers the remaining out-of-pocket hospital bill after PhilHealth and other discounts. DOH Davao says there is no fixed maximum amount, and payment is targeted within 12 working days when documents are complete (2026). Cancer patients at SPMC have used it for laboratories, CT scans, procedures and medicines.

benefits.benefit_name: Remaining medical bill after PhilHealth and other discounts

requirements.requirement_description: Unified Intake Sheet (evaluated by a social worker)
Final bill or statement of account (in-patient), or price quotation and doctor's prescription (out-patient)
Medical certificate or patient's clinical summary / medical abstract
Copy of IDs (patient and/or patient's representative)

procedure.instruction: Ask the hospital's social worker to assess you for MAIFIP. The social worker evaluates your Unified Intake Sheet.
Submit the documents the social worker asks for. Payment is faster when the documents are complete.
